message.content:
I'm auditing the UX of a top-down 3D LLM-NPC town game (C++ / raylib) where TALKING TO NPCs is the core loop. I need a precise, evidence-backed map of the conversation interface and all menus as they exist RIGHT NOW. Report facts only with file:line evidence — no recommendations, just what actually happens.

Read src/app/Menu.cpp/.hpp fully, plus the dialogue/conversation handling in src/app/main.cpp and src/core/LlmClient.* and src/core/Npc.*. Report concretely:
- How does the player START a conversation with an NPC (proximity? key press? what prompt/affordance is shown)?
- How does the player TYPE a message — is there an in-game text input box? How is it rendered, where, character limit, editing (backspace), submit?
- How is the NPC RESPONSE shown — streaming token-by-token (drainDeltas)? A dialogue box? Where on screen, font size, wrapping, how long it stays, how it's dismissed. Is there a conversation history/log visible or just the latest line?
- LATENCY handling: while the LLM is thinking (busy()), is there any indicator — typing dots, "thinking...", spinner? Can the player move/do other things while waiting?
- The full set of menu Pages (Main, Model, Creator, Journal, Multiplayer, etc.): what each contains, how navigation works (mouse click? keyboard?), how the pause menu is opened, layout machinery (Page/Hit/layout).
- Nameplates / who-am-I-talking-to feedback.
- Any conversation affordances: can you end a chat, see who's nearby, re-read what was said.

Give me line-number citations. I especially need to know exactly how repetitive/pleasant the type-a-message-and-read-a-reply loop is, since that's done hundreds of times.

content.text:
I have everything I need. Here is the evidence-backed map.

---

## Conversation & Menu UX Audit — LLM-NPC Town Game

All citations are `file:line`. Files read in full: `Menu.hpp/.cpp`, `LlmClient.hpp/.cpp`, `Npc.hpp/.cpp`, `DialogUI.hpp/.cpp`, `DialogueSession.hpp`, plus the dialogue sections of `main.cpp`.

Note: the actual conversation interface lives in `src/app/DialogUI.cpp` (the transcript + input box) and `src/core/DialogueSession.*` (the state machine), not in `Menu.cpp`. `Menu.cpp` is the pause menu only and never touches conversation.

### 1. Starting a conversation with an NPC

- Trigger is **proximity + a key press**, not proximity alone. Each frame the nearest NPC within `kTalkRadius = 3.5` world units is computed into `nearbyNpc` (`main.cpp:841`, `world.nearestNpcWithin(...)`; constant at `main.cpp:55`).
- Affordance: while in `Playing` mode and an NPC is in range, a centered HUD prompt renders 84px above the screen bottom: `"[" + bindings.key(Action::Talk) + "] Talk to " + npc.persona().name` (`main.cpp:1048-1052`). Default Talk key is **T** (`KeyBindings.cpp:31`).
- Pressing Talk opens the chat only if the NPC is `NpcState::Idle` (not fleeing/hostile/dead) (`main.cpp:565-568`). On open: `session.open(nearbyNpc)`, the NPC turns to face the player via `npc.lookAt(player.position)` (`main.cpp:574`), the dialog is reset/enabled, and a System transcript line is seeded: `"You are talking to " + name + " (" + role + "). Enter sends, Esc leaves."` (`main.cpp:579-581`). Mode switches to `Dialogue` and the mouse cursor is enabled (`main.cpp:582-583`).
- `dialog.swallowPendingText()` (`main.cpp:578`, impl `DialogUI.cpp:109`, `71-80`) discards the frame's keystrokes so the "T" that opened the chat doesn't leak into the input box.

### 2. Typing a message

- Yes, there is an in-game single-line text input box, rendered at the bottom of the screen (`DialogUI::render`, `DialogUI.cpp:193-203`). Box rect: `{kPadding, h - kInputHeight - kPadding*0.5, w - 2*kPadding, kInputHeight}` — full width, `kInputHeight = 48` px tall (`DialogUI.cpp:12-13, 194-195`). Fill color `{30,30,36}`, border `{120,160,220}` when enabled / `{70,70,70}` when disabled (`DialogUI.cpp:196-198`).
- The line renders as `"> " + input_ + "_"` (a literal underscore cursor when enabled) at font size `kFontSize = 16` (`DialogUI.cpp:15, 200-203`). White text when enabled, gray `{120,120,120}` when disabled.
- Input handling in `pollInput()` (`DialogUI.cpp:71-93`): printable ASCII only (`ch >= 32 && ch < 127`) via `GetCharPressed()` (`DialogUI.cpp:74-79`). **No character limit** on the chat input — the input box has no length cap (contrast the Menu/Creator fields which cap at 32/160, `Menu.cpp:205`, and the join address at 64, `Menu.cpp:228`).
- Editing: backspace with key-repeat (`IsKeyPressed(KEY_BACKSPACE) || IsKeyPressedRepeat(KEY_BACKSPACE)`) pops one char (`DialogUI.cpp:83-86`). No left/right cursor movement, no mid-string editing — append/pop-from-end only.
- Submit: `KEY_ENTER` with a non-empty input returns the string and clears the box (`DialogUI.cpp:87-91`). Empty Enter does nothing. There is no send button.
- The submitted line is echoed immediately as a `Player` transcript line labeled `"You"` (`main.cpp:612`), then `npc.ask(submitted)` fires the request (`main.cpp:613`), and the input box is disabled until the reply lands (`dialog.setInputEnabled(false)`, `main.cpp:617`). Guard `!npc.waiting()` (`main.cpp:611`) prevents sending a second line while one is in flight.

### 3. How the NPC response is shown

- **Streaming, token-by-token.** On submit, `dialog.beginStreaming(npc.persona().name)` starts a live line (`main.cpp:616`, impl `DialogUI.cpp:111-115`). Each frame `client.drainDeltas()` is pumped (`main.cpp:845-850`); matching fragments call `dialog.appendStreamingDelta(delta.text)` (`main.cpp:848`), appending to `streamingText_` (`DialogUI.cpp:117-119`).
- The in-progress line renders live at the bottom of the transcript as `speaker + ": " + streamingText_ + "_"` (literal underscore cursor), colored NPC-gold `{255,230,180}` (`DialogUI.cpp:154-162`, color at `DialogUI.cpp:19-20`).
- On completion, `client.drainReplies()` routes the reply (`main.cpp:851-930`). `dialog.endStreaming()` removes the live line (`main.cpp:904`, `DialogUI.cpp:121-125`) and the finalized text is appended as a permanent `Npc` transcript line (`main.cpp:907`). If the model spoke no words but performed an action, a System stage-direction line is shown instead; if truly empty, `"(<name> says nothing.)"` (`main.cpp:909-916`). On error, a System line: `"[<name> seems distracted: <errorMessage>]"` (`main.cpp:924-926`). Then input is re-enabled (`main.cpp:928`).
- Layout/wrapping: it is a **scrolling transcript**, not a single dialogue box. Lines render newest-backward filling the vertical space from `transcriptBottom = h - kInputHeight - kPadding` upward (`DialogUI.cpp:140, 171-191`). Line height `kLineHeight = 22`, font size 16 (`DialogUI.cpp:14-15`). Word-aware wrap to `wrapChars = max(20, (w - 32)/9)` chars/line — a crude fixed-9px-per-char estimate (`DialogUI.cpp:141-142`, `wrap()` at `28-68`).
- History/log: **yes, a visible running transcript** kept in a `std::deque<TranscriptLine>` capped at `kMaxTranscriptLines = 200` (`DialogUI.hpp:58, 68`; `DialogUI.cpp:97-100`). Player lines are blue `{180,220,255}`, NPC gold, System gray (`DialogUI.cpp:17-23`). Behind it a dim overlay `{8,10,16,150}` is drawn (`main.cpp:1088`).
- **No scrollback control** — there is no mouse-wheel or page-up handling anywhere in `DialogUI` or the Dialogue input branch. Only whatever most-recent lines fit on screen are visible; older lines scroll off and cannot be recalled within a session.
- Persistence: the transcript is per-open-session; `dialog.reset()` clears it every time a new conversation opens (`main.cpp:576`, `DialogUI.cpp:127-134`). The NPC's underlying `history_` (capped `maxHistoryTurns=10`, i.e. 20 entries) persists across chats for LLM context (`Npc.hpp:32, 182`; `Npc.cpp:199-206`) but is never shown to the player.
- How long it stays / dismissal: the reply stays as long as the dialog is open; the whole dialog is dismissed by Esc (see §7). Lines are not individually timed.

### 4. Latency handling (while `busy()`)

- There is a "thinking" indicator, but it is driven by the **streaming state**, not `LlmClient::busy()` and not `setThinking()`. `LlmClient::busy()` (`LlmClient.hpp:92`) and `DialogUI::setThinking()` (`DialogUI.cpp:102-105`) both **exist but are never called** anywhere in the app (grep confirms `setThinking` has zero call sites; `busy()` is unused in `main.cpp`).
- The actual indicator: after submit, `beginStreaming` sets `streaming_ = true` with empty `streamingText_`. In `render()`, the branch `else if (thinking_ || streaming_)` fires and draws `"... <speaker> is thinking..."` in gray `{140,140,140}` (`DialogUI.cpp:163-168`). Once the first delta arrives, `streamingText_` is non-empty and it switches to the live streamed text (`DialogUI.cpp:154`). So the player sees "X is thinking..." only until the first token, then live words. It is static text — **no animated dots/spinner** (the dots are the literal string `"... "`).
- Can the player move while waiting? **No, not in the chat.** During `Dialogue` mode the input branch handles only Esc and `pollInput` (`main.cpp:585-620`); WASD movement and combat are gated behind `mode == AppMode::Playing` (`main.cpp:535-557`). The player is frozen in place, cursor visible, staring at the transcript until Esc or the reply. However, the world keeps simulating: NPC behaviors and the day/night clock keep running during dialogue (`main.cpp:648, 651-661` — "NPC behaviors keep running during dialogue, freeze in the menu"). The input box is locked (`setInputEnabled(false)`) so you also cannot queue a next message while waiting.

### 5. The pause menu — Pages, navigation, layout machinery

Opened by `Action::OpenMenu` (default **Escape**) or `KEY_ESCAPE` while in Playing mode; `menu.open()`, mode → `Menu`, cursor enabled (`main.cpp:559-564`). `menu.open()` resets to the Main page and clears edit/toast state (`Menu.cpp:102-109`).

Navigation is **mouse-click only** for buttons (keyboard is used only for text-field typing and Escape). `update()` polls `IsMouseButtonPressed(MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT)`, walks the `layout()` hit-rects, and dispatches by `Hit.id` (`Menu.cpp:253-333`). Escape backs out one page or resumes from Main (`Menu.cpp:245-251`). Clicking empty space cancels captures/edits (`Menu.cpp:328-332`).

**Layout machinery:** `Page` enum {Main, Controls, Multiplayer, Creator, Journal} (`Menu.hpp:100`). A `Hit` is a `Rectangle` + int `id` (`Menu.hpp:103-106`). `layout()` (`Menu.cpp:111-180`) recomputes hit-rects from live `GetScreenWidth/Height()` each call so `render()` and `update()` always agree; `render()` re-calls `layout()` and draws each rect with hover highlight (`Menu.cpp:488-558`). Ids are namespaced by constant blocks (`Menu.cpp:13-38`).

The five pages:
- **Main** (title "Paused", `Menu.cpp:435`): six stacked 320×52 buttons — Resume, Controls, Multiplayer, Create Character, Journal, Quit (`Menu.cpp:116-123, 498-505`). Resume→game, Quit→close (`Menu.cpp:259-260`).
- **Controls**: one chip per action (`kActionCount`) at `w*0.5+90` (`Menu.cpp:171-176`); shows action label + current key; clicking a chip arms `awaiting_` and the next key press rebinds via `applyCapture` (`Menu.cpp:189-198, 338-356`). Instructional line "Click a key, then press the new key. Esc cancels." (`Menu.cpp:483-486`). Rebinds use swap semantics and save to disk immediately (`Menu.cpp:346-355`).
- **Multiplayer**: if a session is active, a Leave button; otherwise Host (fixed port 40605), a click-to-edit join-address field (default `127.0.0.1:40605`, cap 64 chars, Enter joins), and Join (`Menu.cpp:155-169, 225-243, 409-419`). Status line from an injected hook (`Menu.cpp:477-482`).
- **Creator** ("Create a Character"): left column three text fields — Name (required, cap 32), Backstory (cap 160), Traits (cap 160) (`Menu.cpp:130-137, 201-220, 507-518`). Right column: a `[<] label [>]` cycler per body-part category (Body/Head/Eyes/Hair), a Palette cycler, Randomize, and Save & Spawn (`Menu.cpp:140-154, 519-536`). This page dims the overlay less (90 vs 170) because main.cpp renders a live in-world character preview behind it (`Menu.cpp:432`, `Menu.hpp:78-83`). `attemptCreate` validates name and fires the injected `onCreate` hook (`Menu.cpp:388-407`).
- **Journal**: title "Journal"; renders read-only rows from an injected hook, grouped by subject header, 7 rows/page (`kJournalRowsPerPage`), with Prev/Next paging and Back (`Menu.cpp:124-129, 442-475`). Conflicting entries render in orange and are tagged `[conflicting accounts]` (`Menu.cpp:463-467`). Empty state: "You haven't been told anything yet." (`Menu.cpp:446`). This is the only place a player can re-read accumulated NPC-conveyed facts, and it is fact-store data, not conversation transcripts.

Toasts: transient status messages centered at `h*0.88` in yellow, `kToastSeconds = 3` (`Menu.cpp:57, 421-424, 560-562`).

### 6. Nameplates / who-am-I-talking-to feedback

- `drawNameplate()` draws name text at font size **14** with a 1px black shadow, centered on a projected world point (`main.cpp:151-158`).
- Every NPC within `kNameplateRange = 28` units gets a floating nameplate at feet+2.15y (`main.cpp:55-56, 1007-1031`). For local NPCs the plate also appends the current schedule activity: `name + " - " + activity` e.g. "Marge - baking bread" (`main.cpp:1025-1029`; activity from `Npc::activity()`, `Npc.hpp:88`).
- Remote players get cyan nameplates (`main.cpp:1032-1034`); combat callouts float higher in orange (`main.cpp:1036-1045`).
- In-conversation "who am I talking to" feedback: the seeded System line naming the NPC and role (`main.cpp:579-581`) plus every NPC line being prefixed with the speaker name in the transcript (`DialogUI.cpp:173`). There is **no dedicated header/portrait** in the dialog box naming the current partner — you rely on the transcript prefix and the seed line, which can scroll off.

### 7. Conversation affordances (end / who's nearby / re-read)

- **End a chat:** press Esc (`main.cpp:586-597`). It closes the session, ends streaming, returns to Playing, disables the cursor. On close (solo/host) it fires `requestSummary` + `requestFacts` for that NPC (`main.cpp:590-593`) — background LLM calls that update the NPC's persisted memory and extract journal facts; these produce no visible dialog (`main.cpp:853-865`). There is no on-screen "Leave" button in the dialog; Esc is the only exit, and it is only advertised in the seed line ("Esc leaves").
- **See who's nearby:** only the single nearest in-range NPC is surfaced, via the `[T] Talk to <name>` prompt (`main.cpp:1048-1052`) and nameplates (§6). No list of nearby NPCs.
- **Re-read what was said:** within an open chat, only the transcript lines that currently fit on screen are visible; there is no scrollback (§3). Across chats, the transcript is wiped on each new open (`main.cpp:576`). The Journal page (§5) is the only persistent re-readable record, and it holds extracted facts with attribution, not verbatim dialogue.

### The core type-a-message-and-read-a-reply loop (done hundreds of times)

Per message, the mechanical loop is: click/press T to open (mouse cursor toggles on) → type into a single-line box with no length limit and append-only editing (backspace only) → press Enter → input box locks and grays out → "<name> is thinking..." static gray text until first token → tokens stream into a gold line with an `_` cursor → line finalizes into the scrolling transcript → input re-enables. Each turn:
- The player is **rooted in place** the entire time — no movement, no doing anything else while the model thinks (`main.cpp:585-620`, movement gated to Playing at `535`).
- Only **one message can be in flight**; you cannot pre-type the next line (input disabled at `main.cpp:617`, re-enabled only at `928`).
- The "thinking" feedback is **static text, no animation/spinner** (`DialogUI.cpp:163-168`), and the dedicated `busy()`/`setThinking()` plumbing that exists is dead code (never called).
- Exit is **Esc only**, surfaced solely in an easily-scrolled-away seed line.
- There is **no scrollback** to re-read earlier turns mid-conversation, and the transcript is **discarded on every new conversation** (`main.cpp:576`).
- Cursor mode flips every open/close (`EnableCursor`/`DisableCursor` at `main.cpp:583, 597`), so each conversation entails a mouse-mode context switch.
